intro.subtitle: Israel's simplest guide to how elections work. No jargon, promise.

station1.title: Wait, who are you even voting for?
station1.leadMid: — a party with a slate of candidates — not for one person. Behind the curtain waits a stack of slips, one per party. You choose, put it in an envelope, and that's it.
station1.chatQuestion: Wait... so I'm not voting for a prime minister? 😯
station1.chatAnswer: Exactly. No one in Israel directly chooses a prime minister. This whole journey is about that.

station2.title: 120 seats, one pie
station2.lead: The whole country is a single electoral district. Got 10% of the vote? You get about 10% of the seats. That simple.
station2.votesCaption: roughly equal to one seat in the Knesset (a mandate)
station2.accordionContent: The exact seat allocation uses the Bader-Ofer method: a formula that gives a slight edge to relatively larger parties, and lets two parties sign a "surplus agreement" to pool their leftover votes. That's all you need to know to impress people at a dinner party.

station3.title: The electoral threshold
station3.leadStart: A party that doesn't reach at least
station3.leadEnd: of valid votes is left out. And its votes? They evaporate. Not counted for anyone.
station3.statCaption: the minimum entry ticket to the Knesset

about.pageTitle: Who We Are and How the Match Is Calculated
about.pageDescription: Election Compass 2026 is a free, independent tool for checking your match with parties. Learn how the match percentage is calculated, what the distance and direction scores are, and who's behind the project.
about.heading: About Election Compass 2026
about.intro: Election Compass 2026 is a free, independent tool designed to help you understand which parties best represent your views, based on your answers to a position quiz across a range of core topics.

howCalculated.heading: How is the match calculated?
howCalculated.intro: For every question you answer, we compare your position to each party's position, on a scale from -2 (strongly against) to +2 (strongly in favor). The final match percentage is an average of two complementary scores, each capturing a different aspect of "match":
howCalculated.distanceBody: checks how close the actual positions are, number against number: DistanceScore = (1 − Σ(wᵢ × |Uᵢ − Pᵢ|) / Σ(wᵢ × 4)) × 100, where U is your position, P is the party's position, and w is the question's weight.
howCalculated.directionBody: checks something else: whether the overall direction of your positions matches the party's direction across all the questions together, even if the intensity differs (for example: you're "in favor" and the party is "strongly in favor" on the exact same issue). Without this score, a party that consistently takes moderate positions would gain an unfair advantage from the distance score alone, even against someone who clearly matches ideologically with another party that takes more decisive positions.
howCalculated.weightingBody: Parties are ranked from the highest to the lowest match. A question's weight (w) has two components: in the comprehensive track you can mark which topics matter more to you, which produces a higher weight for questions in that category. In addition, every question has a built-in "polarization weight," derived from how much parties actually disagree on it: a question where parties are spread across the whole scale (a genuinely contested issue) affects the result more than a question where almost all parties agree, so the match mainly reflects what actually distinguishes the parties.

privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.body: The entire calculation happens in your browser alone, and the moment you close the page, the answers are deleted.

builders.heading: Who built this
builders.intro: Election Compass 2026 was built as a volunteer effort by two independent entrepreneurs, out of a belief in a free, transparent, and independent tool for the Israeli voter.
builders.thanks: And a heartfelt thank-you to Tova Bani, Ohad's partner, whose belief in this project is the reason it came to be.
